steps.name: TF activity from signed regulons
caveats: Regulon-based activity is inference from target expression, not measured TF binding or protein activity — state this when reporting
TFs with few measured targets in a 12,000-gene matrix produce unstable scores; the >=5-target floor is a minimum, and any top hit with <10 targets should be flagged as low-confidence
Regulon databases are biased toward well-studied TFs; absence of a TF from the ranking may reflect missing curation rather than no activity
With 6 vs 6, per-sample TF activity tests are underpowered — report effect sizes and do not treat a nominal p as confirmation

If a required signed human regulon is unavailable at run time, report that plainly and fall back to the direction-less TF-target sets ONLY as an unsigned over-representation supplement, clearly labelled as such
steps.context: The research question asks which TFs drive the response, which is a TF-activity question rather than a TF-expression question — mineralocorticoid-receptor signalling in kidney acts largely post-translationally, so TF mRNA levels are an unreliable readout. Regulon-based inference reads the TF's activity out of the coordinated behaviour of its targets. The environment holds a curated signed human network (CollecTRI, source/target/weight CSV) and a confidence-graded human alternative (DoRothEA, an .rda carrying tf/confidence/target/mor to be renamed to source/target/weight); both are human, matching taxon 9606. decoupler 2.2.0 is installed in Python; the R decoupleR/dorothea packages are also present if an R route is preferred.
steps.question: Which transcription factors show significantly altered inferred activity in aldosterone-treated versus vehicle kidney samples, and in which direction?
constraints: Use a HUMAN signed regulon — the data is Homo sapiens kidney (taxon 9606); do not substitute a mouse or rat network
Use signed weights; a direction-less TF-target set cannot say whether a TF is activated or repressed and must not be used as the primary prior
Score the per-gene Wald statistic from T1S1 for the contrast-level result — do not score raw counts and do not score only the significant subset
Require >=5 measured targets per TF and report the target count alongside every TF score
BH-adjust TF p-values across all scored TFs and report both nominal and adjusted values
Run the second regulon prior as a cross-check and report agreement/disagreement explicitly rather than silently reporting only the better-looking one
Report per-sample activities and the treated-vs-vehicle test for the top TFs, so each call carries a sample-level effect size and not just a single contrast score
steps.description: Infer TF activity for the aldosterone-vs-vehicle contrast using decoupler with a signed, literature-curated human TF-target regulon network (source TF symbol, target gene symbol, signed weight where +1 is activating and -1 repressing) — resolve it from the environment's regulatory-network reference collection for Homo sapiens. Run TWO complementary analyses. (1) Contrast-level: score the per-gene Wald statistic vector from T1S1 (genes as the single 'sample', TFs as features) with the univariate linear model (ULM) method and, in addition, the consensus of several decoupler methods, giving one signed activity score and p-value per TF for the treated-vs-control contrast. acceptance_criteria: A ranked TF activity CSV with signed score, p, padj, target count and direction for the aldosterone-vs-vehicle contrast
Results from two independent signed human regulon priors, with their top-TF overlap quantified
A 12-sample TF activity matrix plus per-TF treated-vs-vehicle test statistics with BH adjustment
Barplot of top TFs and a condition-annotated per-sample activity heatmap
Explicit written statement of which reference network files were used and their organism

steps.name: Pathway context and MR target check
caveats: The 12,000-gene matrix is smaller than a full transcriptome; pathway coverage will be incomplete and this biases enrichment — report set sizes as measured, not as annotated

With few DE genes, ORA can be dominated by single small sets; check set sizes before interpreting

steps.question: Which pathways are enriched in the aldosterone-vs-vehicle response, and do canonical mineralocorticoid-receptor target genes behave as expected?
constraints: Use human pathway gene sets (HGNC symbols) matching taxon 9606
Use the T1S1 tested-gene list as the ORA background universe, not a default full-genome background
Rank genes for GSEA by the DESeq2 Wald statistic, not by LFC alone and not by p-value magnitude
Report the canonical MR-target table even when nothing reaches significance — absence of movement in these genes is an informative negative
State the significance threshold actually used for the ORA gene lists
steps.description: Contextualize the DE result from T1S1. (a) Run GSEA on the full gene ranking (Wald statistic, descending) against human pathway gene sets resolved from the environment's pathway reference collection (WikiPathways human, HGNC symbols — the descriptor's first field is '%'-delimited, split it to recover a readable set name), and against the human predicted TF-target sets as an unsigned, independent corroboration of the T1S2 TF calls. ORA tables for up- and down-regulated genes with the tested-gene background stated
GTRD TF-target GSEA table usable as an unsigned corroboration of the T1S2 TF ranking
A canonical aldosterone/MR-target gene table showing presence/absence in the matrix, LFC, padj and direction

steps.name: Integrated TF driver report
caveats: Convergent evidence across two regulon priors is not independent — CollecTRI and DoRothEA share curation sources, so agreement is weaker evidence than it appears; say so
If T1S1 found very few DE genes, the TF ranking rests on a weak underlying signal and the whole report must be framed as hypothesis-generating
steps.context: This is the deliverable that answers the user's question directly. The value it adds over T1S2 alone is the cross-evidence reconciliation — a TF whose activity score is high under one prior, absent under the other, and driven by three targets is a different claim from one that is consistent across priors with 40 targets and a matching canonical-pathway story.
steps.question: Which transcription factors are best supported as drivers of the aldosterone response in this 6-vs-6 human kidney dataset, and how strong is the evidence for each?
constraints: Rank by strength of evidence, not by p-value alone; a TF supported by one prior and <10 targets must not outrank a multi-prior, well-covered TF on p-value alone
Report for every shortlisted TF whether its own transcript was measured and whether it moved — and state clearly that TF mRNA change is neither necessary nor sufficient for activity change
Carry forward the exact target counts and adjusted p-values; do not restate scores without their uncertainty
Include the limitations paragraph verbatim in the written output — do not drop it for brevity
Do not assert that any TF causes the response; frame as inferred activity associated with aldosterone treatment
steps.description: Integrate T1S1, T1S2 and T1S3 into a single ranked, evidence-annotated answer to the research question. Build a master table with one row per candidate TF carrying: signed activity score and padj from each regulon prior, number of measured targets, per-sample activity difference between aldosterone-treated and vehicle with its effect size, the TF's own transcript DE statistics from T1S1 (LFC, padj, baseMean, or 'not measured'), whether the TF is corroborated by the unsigned GTRD TF-target enrichment in T1S3, and the leading-edge/driver targets that carry the signal. Write an interpretation that (i) states which TFs are called and in which direction, (ii) says explicitly for each whether the evidence is activity-only, expression-corroborated, or multi-prior consistent, (iii) relates the calls to the canonical MR-axis result from T1S3, and (iv) states the limitations without softening them: n=6 per group, single batch, no replication cohort, regulon-based activity is inference from target expression rather than measured TF occupancy, and regulon databases are biased toward well-studied TFs. acceptance_criteria: A master TF table integrating activity scores from both priors, target counts, per-sample effect sizes, own-transcript DE, and GTRD corroboration
An explicitly ranked shortlist of multi-evidence TF candidates with direction of change
A summary figure combining TF activity with target-level LFC distributions
A written interpretation containing the stated limitations and no causal language

plan.title: Aldosterone vs vehicle kidney: DE + TF activity
plan.analytical_narrative:
The input is a single-batch human kidney bulk RNA-seq experiment: raw Salmon gene-level counts (12,000 genes x 12 samples, gene symbols in the first column of counts.csv) with a 12-row metadata.csv giving condition, 6 aldosterone-treated vs 6 vehicle controls, unpaired. The question — which transcription factors drive the treated-vs-control response — is answered by inferring TF activity from a signed TF-target regulon applied to the differential-expression statistic, not by looking at TF transcript levels (TF mRNA is a poor proxy for TF activity, and mineralocorticoid-receptor signalling in kidney is largely post-translational).

T1S1 runs DESeq2 on the raw counts with ~condition (treated vs vehicle), producing shrunken LFCs and the full per-gene Wald statistic vector, plus VST-transformed values and PCA/sample-distance QC so that any outlier or hidden structure in this n=6-per-group design is visible before interpretation. Gene symbols are the identifier space throughout, which matches the regulon and pathway references.

T1S2 is the core step: decoupler consensus/ULM scoring of the signed human CollecTRI regulon (with human DoRothEA A-C as a cross-check) against the gene-level Wald statistics from T1S1. Running the enrichment on the DE statistic vector — one score per TF for the contrast — is the correct construction for a two-group design; per-sample activities from VST data are also produced so the treated-vs-control separation of each candidate TF can be tested and shown, giving a sample-level effect size rather than a single unreplicated number. Both references are human and confirmed present in the environment, matching taxon 9606.

T1S3 puts the ranked TFs in biological context: over-representation and GSEA of the DE ranking against human WikiPathways and the GTRD TF-target sets, and an explicit check of canonical aldosterone/mineralocorticoid-receptor response genes (SGK1, SCNN1A/B/G, PER1, FKBP5, TSC22D3, KLF15, NR3C1/NR3C2) so the TF calls can be judged against known MR biology rather than accepted on statistics alone.

T1S4 assembles the answer: the ranked TF table with direction, activity score, target coverage, the DE evidence for each TF's own transcript, agreement between the two regulon priors, and the sample-level separation — with explicit statements of the power limits of n=6 per group and of the fact that regulon-based activity is inference from target expression, not measured TF occupancy.
